"""Encoder vs LLM zero-shot -- the model-selection measurement.

EVAL-TIME. Writes ``eval/results/encoder_vs_llm.json``.

Run::

    python eval/ablations/encoder_vs_llm.py --n 60

Model selection is graded on justification, and "the encoder is better calibrated"
is an assertion until something measures it. This compares the two on the five axes
that actually decide the choice:

===============  ===========================================================
axis             why it decides anything
===============  ===========================================================
accuracy         does the cheap model give up quality?
**ECE**          the contribution: is the confidence usable as a threshold?
latency          per email, on the hardware each actually runs on
size / cost      one commits to git and runs free; the other needs a key
resolution       how many distinct confidence values the model can express
===============  ===========================================================

**Sampled, not run over the whole split.** The baseline costs ``k`` API calls per
email, serialised to respect free-tier rate limits. A 520-email split at k=5 is
2,600 calls, which is a rate-limit study rather than a measurement. The sample is
stratified by class so every topic is represented, and ``n`` is reported alongside
every figure.

**The confidence-resolution row is the point.** Self-consistency at k=5 can only
ever return multiples of 0.2, so its reliability diagram has five columns no matter
how much data is collected. The encoder's softmax is continuous. That is not a
tuning difference -- it is why an encoder is the right choice when the threshold is
the product.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import random
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split  # noqa: E402
from eval.metrics.classification import classification_report  # noqa: E402
from triage.models.calibration import expected_calibration_error  # noqa: E402
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber  # noqa: E402


def stratified(rows: tuple[Labelled, ...], n: int, seed: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    """Sample evenly across classes, so no topic is missing from the comparison."""
    by_label: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        by_label[row.label].append(row)

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    per_class = max(1, n // max(len(by_label), 1))
    picked: list[Labelled] = []
    for label in sorted(by_label):
        pool = by_label[label]
        picked.extend(rng.sample(pool, min(per_class, len(pool))))
    rng.shuffle(picked)
    return picked[:n]


def evaluate(classifier: Any, texts: list[str], truth: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a classifier over the sample and score it on every axis."""
    started = time.time()
    predictions = classifier.predict_batch(texts)
    elapsed = time.time() - started

    predicted = [p.label for p in predictions]
    confidences = [p.confidence for p in predictions]
    correct = [p == t for p, t in zip(predicted, truth, strict=True)]
    report = classification_report(truth, predicted)

    return {
        "model": classifier.name,
        "n": len(texts),
        "accuracy": round(report.accuracy, 4),
        "macro_f1": round(report.macro_f1, 4),
        "ece": round(expected_calibration_error(confidences, correct), 4),
        "mean_confidence": round(sum(confidences) / len(confidences), 4),
        "distinct_confidence_values": len({round(c, 4) for c in confidences}),
        "seconds_total": round(elapsed, 1),
        "seconds_per_email": round(elapsed / max(len(texts), 1), 3),
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=60, help="stratified sample size")
    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=5, help="k for self-consistency")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--split", default="test")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=ROOT / "eval" / "results" / "encoder_vs_llm.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier

    rows = stratified(split(args.split), args.n, args.seed)
    scrubber = Scrubber()
    texts = [scrubber.scrub(r.email.text).text for r in rows]
    truth = [r.label for r in rows]
    print(f"comparing on {len(rows)} stratified emails from {args.split!r}")

    encoder = EncoderClassifier()
    print("  encoder ...")
    encoder_result = evaluate(encoder, texts, truth)

    llm_result: dict[str, Any]
    try:
        from triage.llm.client import GroqClient
        from triage.models.llm_zeroshot import build_zeroshot

        baseline = build_zeroshot(tuple(encoder.labels), args.samples, GroqClient())
        print(f"  llm zero-shot (k={args.samples}, {args.n * args.samples} calls) ...")
        llm_result = evaluate(baseline, texts, truth)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- an absent key is a skip, not a failure
        llm_result = {"skipped": True, "reason": str(exc)[:200]}

    artefact = ROOT / "models" / "classifier"
    size_mb = sum(f.stat().st_size for f in artefact.rglob("*") if f.is_file()) / 1024**2

    payload = {
        "split": args.split,
        "n": len(rows),
        "sampling": "stratified by class",
        "seed": args.seed,
        "encoder": {**encoder_result, "runs": "local CPU", "cost": "free",
                    "artefact_mb": round(size_mb, 1), "api_calls": 0},
        "llm_zeroshot": {**llm_result, "runs": "API", "cost": "free tier",
                         "artefact_mb": 0,
                         "api_calls": len(rows) * args.samples,
                         "k": args.samples},
        "reading": (
            "The encoder emits a continuous softmax from one local forward pass. "
            "Self-consistency at k manufactures a distribution from k API calls and "
            "can only express multiples of 1/k, so its confidence resolution is "
            "capped no matter how much data is collected. That is the operational "
            "argument for an encoder when the threshold is the product."
        ),
    }

    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\n{'':22s}{'encoder':>12s}{'llm 0-shot':>13s}")
    for key in ("accuracy", "macro_f1", "ece", "seconds_per_email",
                "distinct_confidence_values"):
        left = encoder_result.get(key, "-")
        right = llm_result.get(key, "skipped")
        print(f"  {key:20s}{left!s:>12}{right!s:>13}")
    print(f"\nwrote {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Encoder vs LLM zero-shot -- the model-selection measurement.

EVAL-TIME. Writes ``eval/results/encoder_vs_llm.json``.

Run::

    python eval/ablations/encoder_vs_llm.py --n 60

Model selection is graded on justification, and "the encoder is better calibrated"
is an assertion until something measures it. This compares the two on the five axes
that actually decide the choice:

===============  ===========================================================
axis             why it decides anything
===============  ===========================================================
accuracy         does the cheap model give up quality?
**ECE**          the contribution: is the confidence usable as a threshold?
latency          per email, on the hardware each actually runs on
size / cost      one commits to git and runs free; the other needs a key
resolution       how many distinct confidence values the model can express
===============  ===========================================================

**Sampled, not run over the whole split.** The baseline costs ``k`` API calls per
email, serialised to respect free-tier rate limits. A 520-email split at k=5 is
2,600 calls, which is a rate-limit study rather than a measurement. The sample is
stratified by class so every topic is represented, and ``n`` is reported alongside
every figure.

**The confidence-resolution row is the point.** Self-consistency at k=5 can only
ever return multiples of 0.2, so its reliability diagram has five columns no matter
how much data is collected. The encoder's softmax is continuous. That is not a
tuning difference -- it is why an encoder is the right choice when the threshold is
the product.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import random
import sys
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from eval.dataset import Labelled, split  # noqa: E402
from eval.metrics.classification import classification_report  # noqa: E402

from triage.models.calibration import expected_calibration_error  # noqa: E402
from triage.pii.scrubber import Scrubber  # noqa: E402


def stratified(rows: tuple[Labelled, ...], n: int, seed: int) -> list[Labelled]:
    """Sample evenly across classes, so no topic is missing from the comparison."""
    by_label: dict[str, list[Labelled]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        by_label[row.label].append(row)

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    per_class = max(1, n // max(len(by_label), 1))
    picked: list[Labelled] = []
    for label in sorted(by_label):
        pool = by_label[label]
        picked.extend(rng.sample(pool, min(per_class, len(pool))))
    rng.shuffle(picked)
    return picked[:n]


def evaluate(classifier: Any, texts: list[str], truth: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a classifier over the sample and score it on every axis."""
    started = time.time()
    predictions = classifier.predict_batch(texts)
    elapsed = time.time() - started

    predicted = [p.label for p in predictions]
    confidences = [p.confidence for p in predictions]
    correct = [p == t for p, t in zip(predicted, truth, strict=True)]
    report = classification_report(truth, predicted)

    return {
        "model": classifier.name,
        "n": len(texts),
        "accuracy": round(report.accuracy, 4),
        "macro_f1": round(report.macro_f1, 4),
        "ece": round(expected_calibration_error(confidences, correct), 4),
        "mean_confidence": round(sum(confidences) / len(confidences), 4),
        "distinct_confidence_values": len({round(c, 4) for c in confidences}),
        "seconds_total": round(elapsed, 1),
        "seconds_per_email": round(elapsed / max(len(texts), 1), 3),
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=60, help="stratified sample size")
    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=5, help="k for self-consistency")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--split", default="test")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=ROOT / "eval" / "results" / "encoder_vs_llm.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from triage.models.encoder import EncoderClassifier

    rows = stratified(split(args.split), args.n, args.seed)
    scrubber = Scrubber()
    texts = [scrubber.scrub(r.email.text).text for r in rows]
    truth = [r.label for r in rows]
    print(f"comparing on {len(rows)} stratified emails from {args.split!r}")

    encoder = EncoderClassifier()
    print("  encoder ...")
    encoder_result = evaluate(encoder, texts, truth)

    llm_result: dict[str, Any]
    try:
        from triage.llm.client import GroqClient
        from triage.models.llm_zeroshot import build_zeroshot

        baseline = build_zeroshot(tuple(encoder.labels), args.samples, GroqClient())
        print(f"  llm zero-shot (k={args.samples}, {args.n * args.samples} calls) ...")
        llm_result = evaluate(baseline, texts, truth)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- an absent key is a skip, not a failure
        llm_result = {"skipped": True, "reason": str(exc)[:200]}

    artefact = ROOT / "models" / "classifier"
    size_mb = sum(f.stat().st_size for f in artefact.rglob("*") if f.is_file()) / 1024**2

    payload = {
        "split": args.split,
        "n": len(rows),
        "sampling": "stratified by class",
        "seed": args.seed,
        "encoder": {**encoder_result, "runs": "local CPU", "cost": "free",
                    "artefact_mb": round(size_mb, 1), "api_calls": 0},
        "llm_zeroshot": {**llm_result, "runs": "API", "cost": "free tier",
                         "artefact_mb": 0,
                         "api_calls": len(rows) * args.samples,
                         "k": args.samples},
        "reading": (
            "The encoder emits a continuous softmax from one local forward pass. "
            "Self-consistency at k manufactures a distribution from k API calls and "
            "can only express multiples of 1/k, so its confidence resolution is "
            "capped no matter how much data is collected. That is the operational "
            "argument for an encoder when the threshold is the product."
        ),
    }

    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\n{'':22s}{'encoder':>12s}{'llm 0-shot':>13s}")
    for key in ("accuracy", "macro_f1", "ece", "seconds_per_email",
                "distinct_confidence_values"):
        left = encoder_result.get(key, "-")
        right = llm_result.get(key, "skipped")
        print(f"  {key:20s}{left!s:>12}{right!s:>13}")
    print(f"\nwrote {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Load ``.env`` into the process environment.

RUNTIME and EVAL-TIME.

``.env.example`` tells a grader to copy the file and fill in their keys, and every
client reads its key from :data:`os.environ`. Without something bridging the two,
a correctly-populated ``.env`` has no effect and the system behaves exactly as it
would with no key at all -- drafting fails on every item, the judge is skipped, and
the failure looks like a missing key rather than a missing loader. That silence is
the reason this module exists rather than being folded into each client.

**Existing environment variables always win.** A value already exported is a
deliberate act -- CI, a container, a one-off override on the command line -- and a
file on disk must not overwrite it. So this fills gaps rather than assigning.

**Never raises.** A missing ``.env`` is normal: keys may come from the real
environment, and the runtime is designed to degrade honestly when a key is absent
(a failed draft escalates carrying its SOP). Turning a missing file into a crash
would take a working degraded path and break it.

No dependency on ``python-dotenv``: the format needed here is a few lines of
``KEY=value``, and parsing it directly keeps one less package in a runtime that has
to install cleanly on a grader's machine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Final

#: Repository root, from this file.
DEFAULT_ENV: Final[Path] = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".env"


def load_env(path: Path | None = None, *, override: bool = False) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read ``KEY=value`` lines into ``os.environ``.

    Args:
        path: The file to read. Defaults to ``.env`` at the repository root.
        override: When True, replace variables already set. Off by default, so an
            exported value beats the file.

    Returns:
        The names that were actually set, mapped to their source. Names only --
        a secret must not be returned to a caller that might log it.
    """
    source = path or DEFAULT_ENV
    if not source.exists():
        return {}

    applied: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in source.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue

        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key = key.strip()
        value = value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        if not key or not value:
            continue

        if override or not os.environ.get(key):
            os.environ[key] = value
            applied[key] = str(source)

    return applied


def key_status() -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Which keys are present, without revealing any of them.

    Printed by entrypoints so a run states up front what it can and cannot do --
    an eval that silently skipped the judge is worse than one that said so.
    """
    return {
        name: bool(os.environ.get(name))
        for name in ("GEMINI_API_KEY", "GROQ_API_KEY", "OPENAI_API_KEY")
    }


__all__ = ["DEFAULT_ENV", "key_status", "load_env"]

"""Provider-agnostic LLM client.

RUNTIME for Gemini (drafting); EVAL-TIME for Groq (the groundedness judge).

One interface over both providers so the draft node and the judge share failure
classification, timeout handling and model-identifier recording. Free-tier rosters
rotate, so the identifier actually used is returned with every response and written
into ``eval/results/`` -- a number that does not record which model produced it
cannot be reproduced later.

**Failures are classified, not just caught.** The draft node's contract is that a
failure reaches the officer as a reason chip (``draft failed: rate limit``), so a
rate limit and a malformed response must be distinguishable here rather than
collapsed into one exception. :class:`LLMError` carries a
:class:`triage.schemas.DraftFailure`, which is the vocabulary the queue renders.

**No retries.** A free-tier rate limit does not clear in the few seconds a retry
would wait, and retrying inside an eval sweep would turn a visible availability
number into a hidden latency cost. Drafting availability is a reported metric
(``BUILD.md`` S6.2), so the failure is surfaced rather than papered over.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Final, Protocol

from triage.schemas import DraftFailure

#: Pinned defaults. Overridable by environment so a rotated free-tier roster does
#: not require a code change.
DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL: Final[str] = "gemini-2.0-flash"
DEFAULT_GROQ_MODEL: Final[str] = "llama-3.3-70b-versatile"

#: Generous enough for a cold free-tier call, short enough that a hung request
#: fails the item rather than stalling a sweep.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: Final[float] = 45.0


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    """A classified provider failure."""

    def __init__(self, reason: DraftFailure, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.reason = reason


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LLMResponse:
    """Generated text plus the identifier of the model that produced it."""

    text: str
    model_name: str


class LLMClient(Protocol):
    """Anything that turns a prompt into text."""

    @property
    def model_name(self) -> str: ...

    def generate(self, prompt: str, *, temperature: float = 0.2) -> LLMResponse: ...


def classify_error(exc: Exception) -> DraftFailure:
    """Map a provider exception onto the reported failure vocabulary.

    Matched on message text rather than exception type because the two SDKs raise
    unrelated hierarchies for the same conditions, and the queue chip needs one
    vocabulary. Anything unrecognised is ``api_error`` -- the honest default, since
    guessing ``rate_limit`` would understate a real outage.
    """
    text = f"{type(exc).__name__} {exc}".lower()
    if any(k in text for k in ("rate limit", "ratelimit", "429", "quota", "resource_exhausted")):
        return DraftFailure.RATE_LIMIT
    if any(k in text for k in ("timeout", "timed out", "deadline")):
        return DraftFailure.TIMEOUT
    return DraftFailure.API_ERROR


class GeminiClient:
    """Google Gemini, free tier -- the drafter.

    The key is read at construction so a missing one fails at startup rather than
    on the first citizen email. In the graph the drafter is constructed lazily, so
    an absent key surfaces as a drafting failure on every item -- which is the
    designed behaviour: the router's decision is unaffected, and the officer
    receives the item with its SOP attached.
    """

    def __init__(self, api_key: str | None = None, model: str | None = None) -> None:
        key = api_key or os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
        if not key:
            raise LLMError(
                DraftFailure.API_ERROR,
                "GEMINI_API_KEY is not set. Copy .env.example to .env and add a key "
                "from https://aistudio.google.com/apikey",
            )
        self._model_name = model or os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL
        self._key = key

    @property
    def model_name(self) -> str:
        return self._model_name

    def generate(self, prompt: str, *, temperature: float = 0.2) -> LLMResponse:
        try:
            import google.generativeai as genai

            genai.configure(api_key=self._key)
            model = genai.GenerativeModel(self._model_name)
            response = model.generate_content(
                prompt,
                generation_config={"temperature": temperature},
                request_options={"timeout": DEFAULT_TIMEOUT},
            )
            text = (response.text or "").strip()
        except LLMError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- classified, then re-raised
            raise LLMError(classify_error(exc), str(exc)) from exc

        if not text:
            # A blocked or empty completion has no text to ground-check, so it is
            # a failure rather than an empty draft the officer would have to spot.
            raise LLMError(DraftFailure.API_ERROR, "provider returned no text")
        return LLMResponse(text=text, model_name=self._model_name)


class GroqClient:
    """Groq, free tier -- the groundedness judge.

    EVAL-TIME ONLY. A different model family from the drafter on purpose: a model
    must not be scored on its own output (``BUILD.md`` S6.4).
    """

    def __init__(self, api_key: str | None = None, model: str | None = None) -> None:
        key = api_key or os.environ.get("GROQ_API_KEY", "")
        if not key:
            raise LLMError(
                DraftFailure.API_ERROR,
                "GROQ_API_KEY is not set. The groundedness judge needs a free key "
                "from https://console.groq.com/keys",
            )
        self._model_name = model or os.environ.get("GROQ_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GROQ_MODEL
        self._key = key

    @property
    def model_name(self) -> str:
        return self._model_name

    def generate(self, prompt: str, *, temperature: float = 0.0) -> LLMResponse:
        try:
            from groq import Groq

            client = Groq(api_key=self._key, timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
            completion = client.chat.completions.create(
                model=self._model_name,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                temperature=temperature,
            )
            text = (completion.choices[0].message.content or "").strip()
        except LLMError:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise LLMError(classify_error(exc), str(exc)) from exc

        if not text:
            raise LLMError(DraftFailure.API_ERROR, "provider returned no text")
        return LLMResponse(text=text, model_name=self._model_name)


__all__ = [
    "DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL", "DEFAULT_GROQ_MODEL", "GeminiClient", "GroqClient",
    "LLMClient", "LLMError", "LLMResponse", "classify_error",
]

"""LLM zero-shot classifier -- the comparison baseline, never the runtime.

EVAL-TIME ONLY. Satisfies the same :class:`triage.models.base.Classifier` Protocol
as the encoder, so the ablation harness swaps them with no special-casing and the
calibration layer is written once.

**Why this exists.** Model selection is graded on justification, and "the encoder is
better calibrated" is an assertion until something measures it. This turns it into a
number: encoder vs LLM on accuracy, latency, size, cost and ECE (``BUILD.md`` S9.3).

**Why it is not the runtime classifier.** The whole contribution is calibration, and
this class is where the difficulty of getting a probability out of a text model is
visible rather than argued about:

* An LLM asked to classify returns *text*. There is no distribution to soften.
* Logprobs would give one, but they are not exposed by every provider and are not
  comparable across them.
* So confidence has to be *manufactured*, and this module does it by
  self-consistency: sample the model ``k`` times at non-zero temperature and read
  agreement as the probability. That costs ``k`` API calls per email, is coarse
  (with k=5 the resolution is 0.2), and its floor is 1/k rather than zero.

The encoder emits a calibratable distribution natively, from one CPU forward pass.
That contrast IS the model-selection argument, and it is why this module is
deliberately built the honest, expensive way rather than by asking the model to
state a confidence -- a self-reported number is not a frequency and would not be
calibratable at all.

**Ordering matters.** ``labels`` is fixed at construction and every distribution is
built over it, so the encoder and this baseline produce vectors that index
identically. Otherwise the two could not be compared.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections import Counter
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Final

from triage.llm.client import LLMClient, LLMError
from triage.schemas import Classification

#: Versioned prompt, on disk beside the drafting one.
PROMPT_PATH: Final[Path] = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "llm" / "prompts" / "classify_zeroshot.v1.txt"
)

#: Samples per email for self-consistency. Five is a compromise the design states
#: rather than hides: enough that agreement means something, few enough that a
#: 520-email test split stays inside a free tier. It caps confidence resolution at
#: 0.2, which is precisely the coarseness the encoder does not suffer from.
DEFAULT_SAMPLES: Final[int] = 5

#: Non-zero, because self-consistency needs the samples to be able to disagree. At
#: temperature 0 every sample is identical and the "distribution" is always 1.0 --
#: which would look like perfect confidence and calibrate to nonsense.
SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE: Final[float] = 0.7

#: Mass reserved for classes the model never named, spread evenly. Without it an
#: unsampled class has probability exactly zero, and a single confident error would
#: give infinite loss under any log-scoring rule.
_SMOOTHING: Final[float] = 0.01


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _prompt_template() -> str:
    return PROMPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


class LLMZeroShotClassifier:
    """Classifies by prompting, with confidence from sample agreement.

    Args:
        client: Any :class:`~triage.llm.client.LLMClient`. Groq by default at the
            call site -- a different family from the drafter, so no model is scored
            on its own output.
        labels: The class set, in the SAME order the encoder uses.
        samples: How many times to sample each email.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        client: LLMClient,
        labels: tuple[str, ...],
        samples: int = DEFAULT_SAMPLES,
        descriptions: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._labels = tuple(labels)
        self._samples = max(1, samples)
        self._descriptions = descriptions or {}

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return f"llm-zeroshot-{self._client.model_name}-k{self._samples}"

    @property
    def labels(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return self._labels

    def _render(self, text: str) -> str:
        catalogue = "\n".join(
            f"- {label}" + (f": {self._descriptions[label]}" if label in self._descriptions else "")
            for label in self._labels
        )
        return _prompt_template().format(labels=catalogue, email=text.strip())

    def _parse(self, reply: str) -> str | None:
        """Pull a known label out of a free-text reply.

        Matched against the known label set rather than trusted verbatim: a model
        that answers "this is a filing question" or invents ``tax_filing`` must not
        create a thirteenth class. An unparseable reply is a non-vote, not a guess.
        """
        lowered = reply.lower()
        if match := re.search(r"^\s*(?:label|answer|class)\s*:\s*([a-z_]+)", lowered, re.M):
            candidate = match.group(1)
            if candidate in self._labels:
                return candidate

        # Fall back to the first label mentioned anywhere, longest-first so that
        # `oos_business_tax` is not shadowed by a shorter overlapping name.
        for label in sorted(self._labels, key=len, reverse=True):
            if label in lowered:
                return label
        return None

    def _distribution(self, votes: list[str]) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Turn sample agreement into a probability distribution.

        Smoothed so no class sits at exactly zero. With no valid votes at all the
        result is uniform -- the honest representation of "this model told us
        nothing", and it routes to low confidence rather than to a fabricated class.
        """
        if not votes:
            return dict.fromkeys(self._labels, 1.0 / len(self._labels))

        counts = Counter(votes)
        floor = _SMOOTHING / len(self._labels)
        scores = {
            label: floor + (1.0 - _SMOOTHING) * counts[label] / len(votes)
            for label in self._labels
        }
        total = sum(scores.values())
        return {label: value / total for label, value in scores.items()}

    def predict(self, text: str) -> Classification:
        prompt = self._render(text)
        votes: list[str] = []

        for _ in range(self._samples):
            try:
                response = self._client.generate(prompt, temperature=SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE)
            except LLMError:
                # A dropped sample is a missing vote, not a wrong one. Losing one
                # of five widens the interval; inventing a vote would bias it.
                continue
            if (label := self._parse(response.text)) is not None:
                votes.append(label)

        scores = self._distribution(votes)
        return Classification(
            label=max(scores, key=lambda k: scores[k]),
            probabilities=scores,
            model_name=self.name,
        )

    def predict_batch(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[Classification]:
        """Classify many emails.

        Sequential on purpose: free-tier limits are per-request-rate, so parallel
        calls would trip them and turn a measurement into a rate-limit study. The
        cost of this baseline -- ``k`` calls per email, serialised -- is itself a
        model-selection finding worth reporting.
        """
        return [self.predict(text) for text in texts]


def build_zeroshot(
    labels: tuple[str, ...],
    samples: int = DEFAULT_SAMPLES,
    client: Any | None = None,
) -> LLMZeroShotClassifier:
    """Construct the baseline against Groq, with taxonomy descriptions if present.

    Descriptions come from ``config/taxonomy.yaml`` so the baseline is told what the
    classes mean in the same words the taxonomy defines them -- otherwise it would
    be guessing from label names and the comparison would be unfair to it.
    """
    if client is None:
        from triage.llm.client import GroqClient

        client = GroqClient()

    descriptions: dict[str, str] = {}
    config = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "config" / "taxonomy.yaml"
    if config.exists():
        import yaml

        document = yaml.safe_load(config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
        for name, spec in (document.get("classes") or {}).items():
            if isinstance(spec, dict):
                text = spec.get("description") or spec.get("scope") or ""
                if text:
                    descriptions[str(name)] = " ".join(str(text).split())[:220]

    return LLMZeroShotClassifier(client, labels, samples, descriptions)


__all__ = ["DEFAULT_SAMPLES", "LLMZeroShotClassifier", "build_zeroshot"]

"""The LLM zero-shot baseline.

Tested with a fake client, so the suite needs no key and no network. What is being
tested is the *manufacturing of a distribution* from text replies -- the part that
makes this baseline defensible as a comparison, and the part that shows why an
encoder is the better runtime choice.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from triage.llm.client import LLMError, LLMResponse
from triage.models.base import Classifier
from triage.models.llm_zeroshot import LLMZeroShotClassifier
from triage.schemas import DraftFailure

LABELS = ("filing", "payment", "tax_reliefs", "account_specific", "oos_business_tax")


class FakeClient:
    """Replays a fixed list of replies, cycling if asked for more."""

    def __init__(self, replies: list[str], model_name: str = "fake-judge") -> None:
        self._replies = replies
        self._model_name = model_name
        self.calls = 0

    @property
    def model_name(self) -> str:
        return self._model_name

    def generate(self, prompt: str, *, temperature: float = 0.2) -> LLMResponse:
        reply = self._replies[self.calls % len(self._replies)]
        self.calls += 1
        return LLMResponse(text=reply, model_name=self._model_name)


class AlwaysFails:
    model_name = "broken"

    def generate(self, prompt: str, *, temperature: float = 0.2) -> LLMResponse:
        raise LLMError(DraftFailure.RATE_LIMIT, "simulated")


def build(replies: list[str], samples: int = 5) -> LLMZeroShotClassifier:
    return LLMZeroShotClassifier(FakeClient(replies), LABELS, samples=samples)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Contract
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def test_satisfies_the_classifier_protocol():
    """The whole point: the ablation harness swaps it for the encoder unchanged."""
    assert isinstance(build(["filing"]), Classifier)


def test_distribution_is_over_the_supplied_labels_in_order():
    result = build(["filing"]).predict("anything")

    assert tuple(result.probabilities) == LABELS


def test_probabilities_sum_to_one():
    result = build(["filing", "payment", "filing"]).predict("anything")

    assert sum(result.probabilities.values()) == pytest.approx(1.0)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Self-consistency: agreement becomes confidence
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def test_unanimous_samples_give_high_confidence():
    result = build(["filing"] * 5, samples=5).predict("How do I file?")

    assert result.label == "filing"
    assert result.confidence > 0.9


def test_split_samples_give_lower_confidence():
    """Three votes to two is genuine uncertainty, and must read as such."""
    result = build(["filing", "filing", "filing", "payment", "payment"], samples=5).predict("x")

    assert result.label == "filing"
    assert 0.5 < result.confidence < 0.7


def test_confidence_resolution_is_capped_by_k():
    """The model-selection argument, as a test.

    With k samples the only reachable confidences are multiples of 1/k. No amount of
    data changes that, which is why the encoder's continuous softmax is the better
    thing to calibrate and threshold.
    """
    seen = set()
    for votes in range(1, 4):
        replies = ["filing"] * votes + ["payment"] * (3 - votes)
        seen.add(round(build(replies, samples=3).predict("x").confidence, 2))

    assert len(seen) <= 3, "resolution should be coarse, bounded by k"


def test_it_costs_k_calls_per_email():
    """Reported as a model-selection finding: k API calls against one CPU pass."""
    client = FakeClient(["filing"])
    LLMZeroShotClassifier(client, LABELS, samples=5).predict("x")

    assert client.calls == 5


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Parsing: a model must not be able to invent a class
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def test_unknown_label_is_not_adopted():
    """``tax_filing`` is not in the taxonomy and must not become a thirteenth class."""
    result = build(["tax_filing"] * 3, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.label in LABELS


def test_prose_reply_is_parsed():
    result = build(["I think this is a filing question."] * 3, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.label == "filing"


def test_longest_label_wins_over_a_shorter_overlap():
    """``oos_business_tax`` must not be shadowed by a shorter name inside it."""
    result = build(["oos_business_tax"] * 3, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.label == "oos_business_tax"


def test_reasoning_block_is_ignored():
    """Reasoning models name several categories while thinking; only the answer counts."""
    reply = "<think>Could be payment or tax_reliefs, hmm.</think>\nfiling"
    result = build([reply] * 3, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.label == "filing"


def test_labelled_answer_format_is_parsed():
    result = build(["Label: payment"] * 3, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.label == "payment"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Degradation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def test_unparseable_replies_give_a_uniform_distribution():
    """Telling us nothing must read as no information, not as a confident guess."""
    result = build(["???"] * 3, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.confidence == pytest.approx(1.0 / len(LABELS))


def test_total_api_failure_gives_uniform_rather_than_raising():
    """A baseline that crashed mid-sweep would lose the whole comparison."""
    result = LLMZeroShotClassifier(AlwaysFails(), LABELS, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.confidence == pytest.approx(1.0 / len(LABELS))


def test_a_dropped_sample_is_a_missing_vote_not_a_wrong_one():
    """Losing one of k widens the interval; inventing a vote would bias it."""
    class SometimesFails:
        model_name = "flaky"

        def __init__(self) -> None:
            self.calls = 0

        def generate(self, prompt: str, *, temperature: float = 0.2) -> LLMResponse:
            self.calls += 1
            if self.calls == 2:
                raise LLMError(DraftFailure.RATE_LIMIT, "simulated")
            return LLMResponse(text="filing", model_name="flaky")

    result = LLMZeroShotClassifier(SometimesFails(), LABELS, samples=3).predict("x")

    assert result.label == "filing"
    assert result.confidence > 0.9, "two agreeing votes out of two counted"


def test_no_class_has_exactly_zero_probability():
    """Smoothed, so a single confident error is not infinitely penalised."""
    result = build(["filing"] * 5, samples=5).predict("x")

    assert all(p > 0 for p in result.probabilities.values())


def test_name_records_the_model_and_k():
    """A result that does not say which model produced it cannot be reproduced."""
    name = build(["filing"], samples=4).name

    assert "fake-judge" in name
    assert "k4" in name

content.text:
Done. Lint clean, 305 tests pass, committed.

## Your questions

**The `Email` thing** — not a bug in your code, a mistake in mine. Your `extra="forbid"` is correct and worth keeping: a real inbound email has no `label` field, so if `Email` accepted extras a node could read `email.label`, score brilliantly in eval, and be impossible in production. Forbidding extras turns that into a crash at the seam instead of an inflated number. `eval/dataset.py` keeps ground truth in a sibling object (`Labelled.email` / `Labelled.label`), so the runtime path physically can't reach it.

**Drafting temperature** — `0.2`, set in `llm/client.py`. Low because the drafter must stay inside the SOP's approved phrasing. The judge runs at `0.0` for reproducible verdicts.

## The triggers — my earlier framing was wrong

I called them "unwired flags." They're actually **misfile guards**, which is a different thing, and answering your question properly changed how I built them.

- **`foreign_income_dta`** — yes, held out. `SOP-INC-001`/`INC-002` are both `indexed: false`. `SOP-RES-001` (residency, auto-answerable) declares it because the two share vocabulary — both are about living/working across a border.
- **`scam_report`** — **not** held out. It has `SOP-ESC-003` and routes to `high_consequence`. `SOP-RTE-002` declares it because a redirect SOP could send a fraud victim off to another agency.

So they only matter when the classifier is **wrong**, in the unsafe direction:

| Email really is | Classifier says | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| foreign income | `residency` | auto-replies from residency SOP | escalates |
| scam report | `oos_other_agency` | redirects to another agency | escalates |

Both now wired, keyed to the frontmatter triggers so the corpus still decides. On the test split: **`scam_signal` P 1.000 / R 0.976**, **`foreign_income_signal` P 1.000 / R 0.762**. Zero false positives across 520 emails, so they cost no coverage. Headline numbers are unchanged — these stop specific misfiles being auto-answered, they don't fix accuracy.

`hardship_or_waiver` stays deferred per S10, and there's now a test asserting every flag keys on a trigger some indexed SOP actually declares.

## Your other agent's changes

`route.py`, `flags.py`, `calibration.py` — all three check out. Same structure, and I verified behaviourally: thresholds load correctly, the `$4,000 per child` published-figure case still correctly does *not* fire the computation flag, and the threshold clamp from S9.9 is intact.

## Two things I found while doing this

**`.env` was never loaded.** Your `GROQ_API_KEY` is populated but nothing read it, so the process behaved exactly as keyless — judge skipped, every draft failed. Added `triage/env.py`; existing env vars still win.

**Groq withdrew `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`.** Every call was 404ing. Your design handled it correctly — dropped votes fell back to uniform rather than fabricating — but silently. Repinned to `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, chosen over the `openai/gpt-oss-*` models also on the roster because GPT-4o wrote your corpus and a judge from that family weakens separation rule 3.

## One result you should look at

The baseline runs, and on a 36-email stratified sample it **beats your encoder**:

| | encoder | LLM 0-shot |
|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.667 | **0.833** |
| ECE | 0.308 | **0.124** |
| sec/email | **0.63** | 8.64 |
| distinct confidences | **36** | 2 |

The last row still carries your architectural argument — resolution capped at 1/k regardless of data. But "the encoder is better calibrated" isn't currently true, and that's downstream of the undertrained classifier rather than of the design. Worth deciding how you want to handle that before it goes in the writeup.

# Architecture Audit

## ✅ Complete and verified sound

**`src/triage/schemas.py`** (476 lines) — The strongest file. Invariants enforced in validators, not control flow: always-escalate buckets can't produce an auto-reply, escalated items must carry a reason, redirects only for `out_of_scope`. `redacted()` is a real persistence boundary.

**`src/triage/graph.py`** (232) — Six nodes, one conditional edge, DI via `GraphDeps`. Verified: a total classifier crash escalates to `no_supporting_sop` with `in_human_queue: True` rather than guessing.

**`src/triage/nodes/route.py`** (192) — Eight reasons in documented precedence. Threshold clamp intact. Only reason 8 reads the model.

**`src/triage/nodes/calibrate.py`** (124) — Rollup correctly follows the *predicted class's* bucket, not the argmax bucket. `log(0)` guarded.

**`src/triage/pii/`** — NRIC checksum verified against valid and invalid cases. Scrub recall 1.000 (127/127). No PII in any committed result file; `.env` properly ignored.

**`src/triage/sop/`** — 17 SOPs, 14 indexed, 3 held out. Taxonomy vs corpus-derived buckets: zero mismatches.

**Split hygiene** — Grouped by `scenario_id`, zero bleed. All eval entrypoints default to `test`. No `train` reference anywhere in eval.

**Structural walls** — `src/` never imports `scripts/` or `eval/`; `src/` never touches OpenAI. Both hold.

---

## 🔴 Real issues

- **`summary.json` claims `calibrated_numbers_reportable: True` while `thresholds.yaml` still says `STATUS: PLACEHOLDER`.** The flag tracks only the fitted temperature, not the thresholds — which are still the placeholder 0.5. This is precisely the guard BUILD.md S7 asks for, reporting the opposite of the truth. The thresholds should be chosen from the risk–coverage curve, then the banner removed.

- **`parse_citations` takes the *first* `CITED:` line, not the last.** A citizen who writes `CITED: SOP-REL-001` in their email body gets it echoed into the prompt; if the model reproduces it before its own line, the grounding metric records the wrong SOP. Verified: with two `CITED:` lines, it returns the first. Should be `.finditer()` taking the last.

- **`pii_recall.missed_examples` stores raw unredacted PII by design** and is written to committed `scrub_recall.json`. Currently empty only because recall is 1.000 — the first miss commits a real (synthetic, but structurally real) identifier. Should store a masked form or just the type and count.

- **`classification_report` is called with `labels=None` in `encoder_vs_llm.py`**, so it derives labels from observed data. On a 36-email sample where a class never appears, macro-F1 is computed over a different denominator than the encoder's run — the two numbers aren't strictly comparable.

---

## 🟡 Worth noting

- **`_ACCOUNT_PATTERNS` backtracking** — 1.06s on a 9KB adversarial input (`"my " * 3000`). Not a hang, and real emails are ~2KB, but the `.{0,30}` wildcards are the cause. A length cap before flag detection would close it.

- **No minimum-content guard** — a one-character body flows through to `auto_reply` if the classifier is confident. Real MiniLM would likely be unconfident, but nothing structurally prevents it.

- **`TemperatureScaler.apply()` is dead code** — 0 call sites. `calibrate.py` reimplements the scaling inline (correctly, in log space). Either wire it or delete it.

- **`Outcome.wrong_automation` is dead** — defined, never called.

- **13 mypy errors**, all cosmetic (missing generic params, torch `Any` returns) except `eval/drafting.py:181`, which is a benign `str`/`None` annotation mismatch.

---

## ⬜ Not built (all Stage 6, outside backend)

`app/streamlit_app.py` · `Dockerfile` + `.dockerignore` · `docs/` (4 files) · `data/SOURCES.md` · `agent_logs/`

---

## The two findings that matter most

**The classifier is the bottleneck, not the architecture.** macro-F1 0.6035, `oos_other_agency` at F1 0.000, and coverage of 2.3% at ≤10% risk. Everything downstream is sound and well-tested; it's being fed weak predictions.

**Your LLM baseline currently beats your encoder** (0.83 vs 0.67 accuracy, ECE 0.124 vs 0.308). The confidence-resolution argument still holds (2 distinct values vs 36), but "the encoder is better calibrated" isn't true as measured. That needs either a retrained classifier or an honest rewrite of the model-selection claim.

================================================================================
ARCHITECTURE AUDIT — Calibrated Triage Agent
================================================================================

Date:     2026-09-02
Scope:    Backend only. src/triage/, eval/, config/, tests/. Stage 6 deliverables
          (Streamlit, Docker, docs/) are not built and are listed in section 8
          rather than reported as defects.
Method:   Static (ruff, mypy), dynamic (287→305 pytest), and adversarial probing.
          Every finding below was reproduced at the command line; none is
          inferred from reading alone. Line numbers are as of this date.

Verified state at time of audit:
    ruff .................. all checks passed (src, eval, scripts, tests)
    pytest ................ 305 passed
    mypy .................. 13 errors, all cosmetic except one (see 4.4)
    test suite size ....... 2,430 lines across 8 files
    eval corpus ........... 520 test emails, 12 classes


================================================================================
1. SUMMARY
================================================================================

The architecture is sound. The layering the design argues for — corpus-derived
policy, a single escalation gate, calibration at bucket level, drafting as the
only fallible node — is implemented as described, and the invariants that matter
are enforced structurally rather than by convention.

Four real defects were found. None is a design flaw; all four are localised and
each is a few lines to fix. Two of them (3.1, 3.2) would produce a WRONG NUMBER
IN THE WRITEUP rather than a crash, which makes them the most serious kind of
bug this project can have — the failure mode BUILD.md's "eval/results/ is
committed" rule exists to prevent.

The dominant risk to the submission is not in this list. It is that the
classifier is undertrained (macro-F1 0.6035, one class at F1 0.000) while every
component around it is sound. See section 7.


================================================================================
2. WHAT IS COMPLETE AND VERIFIED
================================================================================

2.1 src/triage/schemas.py — 476 lines
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The strongest file in the repository. Its distinguishing property is that the
routing invariants are enforced in pydantic validators rather than in the
router's control flow, so a future edit to route.py cannot violate them without
raising.

Verified enforced:
  - _always_escalate_buckets_escalate: REQUIRES_ACCOUNT_LOOKUP, HIGH_CONSEQUENCE
    and NO_SUPPORTING_SOP cannot construct a non-escalate decision at ANY
    confidence, including 1.0.
  - _reason_matches_action: an escalated item must carry a reason; a non-escalated
    one must not.
  - _redirect_only_for_out_of_scope: REDIRECT is unavailable to any other bucket,
    and AUTO_REPLY unavailable outside auto_answerable.
  - _check_distribution: probabilities must sum to 1.0 within 1e-3, and the
    predicted label must exist in the distribution.

The Email/ground-truth separation is correct and worth keeping. Email declares
extra="forbid", so a corpus row (which carries label, source_sops, plant_pii and
eight other generation fields) cannot be loaded as an Email. This is deliberate:
a real inbound citizen email has no `label` field, so if Email accepted extras a
node could read email.label, score perfectly in evaluation, and be impossible to
deploy. Forbidding extras converts that mistake into an immediate failure at the
seam instead of an inflated metric. eval/dataset.py holds ground truth in a
SIBLING object (Labelled.email / Labelled.label), so the runtime path cannot
reach it even accidentally.

redacted() is a genuine persistence boundary: it substitutes the scrubbed text,
empties the vault, drops the sender, and — importantly — falls back to blanking
the body entirely when scrubbing never ran, rather than passing the original
through on the assumption it was clean.

2.2 src/triage/graph.py — 232 lines
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    scrub -> classify -> calibrate -> retrieve -> route -+-> draft    -> END
                                                         +-> declined -> END

Six nodes, one conditional edge, dependencies injected via GraphDeps so nodes
stay pure(state) -> partial state and tests construct graphs with stubs and no
weights on disk.

The conditional edge is the escalation gate made structural: an escalated item
does not reach the drafting node because NO EDGE LEADS THERE, not because of an
early return inside the drafter that a later edit could delete.

Fail-safe verified by injecting a classifier that raises:
    classifier crash -> escalate | no_supporting_sop | in_human_queue: True
    errors: ['classify failed: model died',
             'calibrate skipped: no classification',
             'retrieve skipped: no classification',
             'routed without a prediction: escalating']
    draft: not_attempted
Each node degrades independently, records why, and the item reaches a human.
Nothing guesses.

2.3 src/triage/nodes/route.py — 192 lines
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Eight escalation reasons in documented precedence. Reasons 1-7 are structural and
would fire identically at probability 1.0; only reason 8 (low_confidence) reads
the model. The threshold clamp from BUILD.md S9.9 is intact — verified that a
sweep multiplier of 1.5 does not raise.

2.4 src/triage/nodes/calibrate.py — 124 lines
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Contains the subtlest correct decision in the codebase, and it is worth stating
because it is easy to get wrong and impossible to notice when wrong:

    The predicted bucket is the bucket of the PREDICTED CLASS, not the argmax of
    the summed bucket distribution.

These differ. An email at account_specific 0.40 with three auto-answerable
classes at 0.20 each has an auto_answerable bucket mass of 0.60 — larger than
the 0.40 on the bucket that actually applies. Taking the argmax bucket would
auto-reply to an enquiry about a real taxpayer's record. The code follows the
class; test_rollup_follows_the_class_not_the_argmax_bucket pins it.

log(0) is guarded via _EPSILON for buckets holding no probability mass.

2.5 src/triage/pii/ — scrubber.py 171, nric.py 75
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - NRIC checksum verified against valid (S0433218J, G2720465T, S1234567D) and
    invalid (S0000000A, X1234567A, S123456D) inputs. All six correct.
  - Scrub recall on the test split: 1.0000 (127/127 planted values).
  - No PII in ANY committed file under eval/results/ — all 11 JSON files scanned
    for NRIC and SG phone patterns, zero hits.
  - .env is untracked and correctly matched by .gitignore line 7.
  - Rehydration happens in exactly one place (draft.py) and only after the
    network call.

2.6 src/triage/sop/ — loader.py 197, index.py 142
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
17 SOPs; 14 indexed, 3 held out (SOP-INC-001, SOP-INC-002, SOP-REL-005).
config/taxonomy.yaml vs corpus-derived buckets: ZERO mismatches across all 12
classes. The holdout works by derivation — an empty CLASS_TO_SOPS lookup IS the
no_supporting_sop signal, so holding out a further SOP needs no code change.

Loader validation is strict and fails at startup: missing frontmatter keys,
synthetic != true, empty intents, and empty references are all hard errors. The
synthetic banner check is a structural guard against the misrepresentation
failure mode, not decoration.

2.7 eval/ — 12 files, ~2,050 lines
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Single entrypoint (run_eval.py) writing 11 committed artefacts plus 2 PNGs.

Split hygiene verified clean:
  - All three eval entrypoints default to --split test.
  - No reference to the "train" split anywhere in eval/ outside dataset.py.
  - Temperature is fitted on `calibration` (scripts/fit_calibration.py) and
    reported on `test` (run_eval.py). No crossover.

The risk-coverage sweep calls the REAL router at each of 37 multipliers rather
than reimplementing the decision rule, so the published curve cannot drift from
the system it describes. Classification runs once; only routing is re-run.

2.8 Structural walls
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Both walls BUILD.md S4.1 requires were checked by grep and hold:
  - src/ never imports scripts/ or eval/         (0 matches)
  - src/ never references OpenAI (paid, build-time only)  (0 matches)
The runtime therefore stays free-tier and reproducible on a grader's own key.

2.9 The two misfile guards (added this session)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
foreign_income_dta and scam_report were declared in SOP frontmatter but
unenforced. Both are now wired. Measured on the 520-email test split:

    foreign_income_signal   P 1.000   R 0.762   support 42
    scam_signal             P 1.000   R 0.976   support 42

Precision 1.000 on both means zero false positives, so they cost no coverage.
They are misfile guards rather than cross-cutting conditions: they matter only
when the classifier puts an email in the WRONG class, in the direction where
that error is unsafe (auto-answering a held-out foreign-income question from the
residency SOP; redirecting a fraud victim to another agency).

Note: these do NOT require retraining the classifier. flags.py is pure regex over
text and the router consults it after classification. The weights and the
12-class label set are untouched. This is BUILD.md S9.4's separation working as
intended — policy changes without a retrain.

hardship_or_waiver remains the only declared-but-unwired trigger, which is the
documented S10 deferral, and tests/test_schemas.py now asserts that every wired
flag keys on a trigger some indexed SOP actually declares.


================================================================================
3. REAL DEFECTS — fix before reporting any number
================================================================================

3.1 summary.json asserts reportability that config/thresholds.yaml denies
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY: high — this is the exact failure BUILD.md S7 exists to prevent.
LOCATION: eval/run_eval.py:330

    "calibrated_numbers_reportable": scaler.fitted,

The flag is set from scaler.fitted alone, which is True because the temperature
WAS fitted (T=0.6831, n=401). But config/thresholds.yaml line 15 still reads:

    # STATUS: PLACEHOLDER. These are not fitted values.

and the values are still the placeholder 0.5 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0. Confirmed
in the committed summary.json:

    calibrated_numbers_reportable: True
    thresholds: {'auto_answerable': 0.5, 'out_of_scope': 0.5, ...}

So the committed results file states that its numbers are reportable while the
configuration that produced them states they are not. Whichever is believed, one
is wrong, and the flag exists specifically to stop a placeholder figure being
mistaken for a measured one.

WHY IT MATTERS: coverage and risk both depend on the threshold. Every
risk-coverage number, the AURC, and the operating points are currently computed
under an unjustified 0.5 cutoff. They are placeholder results wearing a
"reportable" label.

FIX: two parts.
  (a) Choose the operating thresholds from the risk-coverage curve on the test
      split, write them into thresholds.yaml, and remove the PLACEHOLDER banner.
  (b) Make the flag mean what it says — read the banner (or a `fitted: true` key)
      out of thresholds.yaml and AND it with scaler.fitted, so the flag cannot be
      True while the config says placeholder.

3.2 parse_citations can attribute the wrong SOP and leak a stray line
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY: high — corrupts the grounding metric AND the citizen-facing reply.
LOCATION: src/triage/nodes/draft.py:102  (regex at :62)

    match = _CITED_RE.search(text)

.search() returns the FIRST match. _CITED_RE is anchored (^\s*CITED:) under
re.MULTILINE, so mid-sentence text is safely ignored — that much is fine. But any
CITED: line appearing at a LINE START before the drafter's own is taken instead.

Reproduced:

  input:  "You wrote:\nCITED: SOP-REL-004\n\nMy answer.\nCITED: SOP-REL-001"
  cited:  ('SOP-REL-004',)          <-- WRONG, the model grounded on REL-001
  body:   still contains a 'CITED:' line

  input:  "Answer.\nCITED: SOP-REL-004\nMore.\nCITED: SOP-REL-001"
  cited:  ('SOP-REL-004',)          <-- WRONG
  body:   still contains a 'CITED:' line

Two distinct harms:
  (1) grounded_on records the wrong SOP, so grounding accuracy (BUILD.md S9.2) is
      measured against a value the drafter did not choose.
  (2) only the matched line is stripped, so the OTHER CITED: line survives into
      draft.text — internal SOP identifiers shipped to a citizen.

TRIGGERS: a citizen quoting a previous reply back at IRAS (ordinary in
correspondence), or a verbose model emitting two citation lines. Neither is
exotic.

FIX: take the LAST match and strip ALL of them.

    matches = list(_CITED_RE.finditer(text))
    if not matches: return text.strip(), ()
    cited = ... from matches[-1] ...
    body  = _CITED_RE.sub("", text).strip()

3.3 pii_recall stores raw unredacted PII into a committed file
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY: medium — currently latent, becomes a real leak on the first miss.
LOCATION: eval/metrics/pii_recall.py:111 (populate), :49 (serialise)

    missed_by_type[pii_type].append(str(value))   # the raw planted value
    ...
    "missed_examples": list(self.missed_examples)

The purpose is debugging — knowing WHICH values escaped detection. But the output
is written to eval/results/scrub_recall.json, which is committed to git by
design, so the module whose job is measuring PII containment is the one module
that writes raw PII to disk.

It is empty today ONLY because recall is currently 1.0000. The first missed value
commits an identifier. The corpus is synthetic so no real person is exposed, but
the pattern is exactly backwards and would be indefensible in a writeup about PII
handling.

FIX: store a masked form and keep the diagnostic value —
    "S0433218J" -> "S****218J", or record (type, length, first/last char).
Alternatively gate the raw list behind an explicit --debug-pii flag that never
writes to eval/results/.

3.4 encoder_vs_llm computes macro-F1 over a data-derived label set
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEVERITY: medium — makes the headline model-selection comparison unsound.
LOCATION: eval/ablations/encoder_vs_llm.py:87

    report = classification_report(truth, predicted)     # labels= omitted

With labels omitted, classification_report derives the label set from the union
of truth and predictions actually seen. On a small stratified sample the two
models see DIFFERENT label sets — a class the encoder never predicts but the LLM
does (or vice versa) changes the macro denominator — so the two macro-F1 figures
are averages over different numbers of classes and are not comparable.

Quantified:
    derived labels ('filing','payment')               -> macro_f1 0.3333
    fixed   labels ('filing','payment','tax_reliefs') -> macro_f1 0.2222
    discrepancy 0.1111 on the same predictions

This directly affects the encoder-vs-LLM table, which is the evidence for the
model-selection deliverable.

FIX: pass the fixed 12-class set to both calls —
    classification_report(truth, predicted, labels=tuple(encoder.labels))


================================================================================
4. LOWER-SEVERITY FINDINGS
================================================================================

4.1 Quadratic backtracking in the currency-question pattern
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOCATION: src/triage/nodes/flags.py:71  (_CURRENCY_QUESTION)

NOTE — this corrects an earlier verbal report in which I attributed the slowdown
to _ACCOUNT_PATTERNS. Isolating each pattern individually shows the account
patterns are fast; _CURRENCY_QUESTION is the sole cause.

The [^.?!]* segments on either side of the first-person marker backtrack against
input with no sentence terminator. Measured on "my " * n + "refund?":

        n_words   seconds
            750     0.060
           1500     0.257
           3000     0.999
           6000     4.619

Clean quadratic — doubling the input quadruples the time. Real citizen emails are
~2KB and complete in milliseconds, so this is not a live problem; it is a
denial-of-service shape in a public-facing intake path, which is a different
thing from a bug.

FIX (cheapest): cap the text length before flag detection, e.g. detect_flags
operates on text[:4000]. A citizen email longer than that is already anomalous.
Alternatively bound the wildcards — [^.?!]{0,200} — which preserves intent, since
a first-person marker 200+ characters from the currency figure is not the
"whose facts" signal the pattern is trying to catch.

4.2 No minimum-content guard
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A one-character body ("x") flows through the whole pipeline and reaches
auto_reply if the classifier is confident. Verified with a stub forcing 0.9.

The real MiniLM would probably be unconfident on such input and the threshold
would catch it — but that is a hope about model behaviour, not a property. Every
other safety rule in this system is structural, and this one is not.

FIX: escalate below a minimum token count with a new reason (insufficient_content),
or document explicitly that the confidence threshold is the intended guard.

4.3 Dead code
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - TemperatureScaler.apply()  (models/calibration.py:57) — 0 call sites.
    nodes/calibrate.py reimplements the scaling inline, correctly, in log space.
    Having two implementations of the contribution's core transformation, one
    unused, invites a future edit to the wrong one. Either wire it or delete it.
  - Outcome.wrong_automation  (eval/metrics/risk_coverage.py:47) — defined, never
    called.
  - eval/dataset.py iter_splits — defined, used only in its own module.

4.4 mypy — 13 errors
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Twelve are cosmetic: missing generic parameters (StateGraph), torch functions
returning Any, and two unused type: ignore comments. One is a genuine annotation
mismatch:

    eval/drafting.py:181 — drafter_error declared str, assigned None on the
    success branch. Benign at runtime; should be str | None.

4.5 The judge's agreement figure is not yet computed
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
eval/drafting.py reports the Groq verdict rate but carries a note that
judge-human agreement is "reported separately once the drafts are hand-reviewed."
BUILD.md S6.3 is explicit that agreement is what makes the judge defensible
rather than decorative. Until the ~50 sampled drafts are hand-labelled, the
groundedness number should not be presented as validated.


================================================================================
5. SECURITY REVIEW
================================================================================

Checked and CLEAN:

  Prompt injection via email body — SAFE. Email text is passed as an ARGUMENT to
  str.format(), never as part of the template, so braces in a body are inert.
  Verified with bodies containing "{sops}", "{}", "{0}" and "{x}" — none raised
  or interpolated. (This is worth keeping in mind if anyone later switches to
  f-strings or .format on user-supplied templates, which would break it.)

  Label injection via the LLM baseline — SAFE. _parse matches replies against the
  known label set, so a model answering "tax_filing" cannot create a thirteenth
  class. Reasoning blocks (<think>...</think>) are stripped before parsing so a
  model's deliberation, which names several categories, cannot be mistaken for
  its conclusion.

  Placeholder fabrication — SAFE and deliberate. A draft containing a placeholder
  the vault never issued (e.g. [NRIC_7]) fails the draft rather than shipping a
  bare token. Covered by test_fabricated_placeholder_fails_the_draft.

  Secret handling — CLEAN. .env untracked and gitignored; env.py returns only
  variable NAMES, never values; key_status() reports booleans. No key is logged
  or serialised.

  Committed artefacts — CLEAN. All 11 JSON files under eval/results/ scanned for
  NRIC and SG phone patterns: zero hits.

Residual risks, both stated rather than fixed:

  - PII detection is regex plus a street gazetteer. Free-text addresses without a
    street-type token are the known gap. Recall is MEASURED (1.0000 on planted
    values) rather than claimed, which is the right posture — but planted PII is
    PII the generator knew to plant, so this measures detection of known shapes,
    not of everything a citizen might write.
  - See 3.3 — the module measuring containment currently writes raw values.


================================================================================
6. TEST COVERAGE
================================================================================

305 tests, 2,430 lines across 8 files. All passing.

    test_schemas.py ......... invariants, enums, redaction boundary
    test_router.py .......... escalation logic (highest-value)
    test_scrubber.py ........ PII detection and rehydration
    test_sop_corpus.py ...... corpus structure and validation
    test_graph_smoke.py ..... 11 — wiring, conditional edge, every class routes
    test_draft_failure.py ... 17 — the auto_reply_intended invariant
    test_calibration.py ..... rollup, monotonicity, ECE
    test_llm_zeroshot.py .... 17 — self-consistency, parsing, degradation

Gaps worth closing:

  - No test covers the multi-CITED case in 3.2. Add one alongside the fix.
  - No test asserts the reportability flag agrees with thresholds.yaml (3.1).
  - No test for pii_recall's serialisation (3.3).
  - No adversarial-length test for flags (4.1).

All four are regression tests for the defects above and should land with the
fixes rather than separately.


================================================================================
7. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST
================================================================================

Everything in sections 3 and 4 is localised and cheap. The real problem is
elsewhere and is not an architecture problem:

    macro-F1 (12 classes) ......... 0.6035
    oos_other_agency .............. F1 0.000 over 41 test examples
    payment ....................... F1 0.257
    coverage at <=10% risk ........ 2.3%

A class that is never once predicted correctly across 41 examples is a training
failure, not a weak class. Investigated and ruled out: label alignment is correct
(labels.json is sorted, matching train_encoder.py), and the splits are clean
(grouped by scenario_id, zero bleed). The signature is undertraining —
training.json shows calibration accuracy plateauing at epoch 3 (0.7357) and
FALLING at epoch 4 (0.7282) with train loss still at 0.98.

The consequence for the writeup is direct: coverage of 2.3% at a 10% risk
tolerance does not support a claim that a meaningful share of the inbox can be
automated. The mechanism is sound and well-tested; it is being fed weak
predictions.

Related, and awkward: the LLM zero-shot baseline currently BEATS the encoder.

                        encoder    llm 0-shot
    accuracy             0.667        0.833
    macro-F1             0.655        0.826
    ECE                  0.308        0.124
    sec/email            0.631        8.643
    distinct conf vals      36            2

(n=36 stratified, k=3. Subject to 3.4 — recompute with a fixed label set.)

The architectural argument survives: 2 distinct confidence values against 36 is
the resolution cap at 1/k, which no amount of data removes, and that is the real
case for an encoder when the threshold is the product. But "the encoder is better
calibrated" is currently FALSE as measured, and the writeup cannot assert it.
Either the classifier is retrained, or the model-selection section is rewritten
around the resolution/latency/cost argument and reports the accuracy gap
honestly.

One further note for the build log: the fitted temperature is 0.6831, which
SHARPENS rather than flattens. This is the opposite of BUILD.md S5.5's premise
that raw softmax is overconfident. The cause is the 12->5 rollup: probability
mass scattered across several classes within one bucket sums to an
UNDER-confident bucket score. Worth recording as a genuine finding — it is a
consequence of the bucket design that the design did not anticipate.


================================================================================
8. NOT BUILT — Stage 6, outside the backend
================================================================================

    app/streamlit_app.py .......... the officer's two-queue demo
    Dockerfile, .dockerignore ..... clean-machine reproducibility
    docs/DEVELOPMENT_NARRATIVE.md
    docs/MODEL_SELECTION.md ....... should absorb section 7's finding
    docs/DEPLOYMENT.md
    docs/LIMITATIONS.md ........... should absorb 4.1, 4.2, 5's residual risks
    data/SOURCES.md ............... provenance, licence, fetch dates
    agent_logs/ ................... BUILD.md stage 0

config/models.yaml WAS missing and has been added, including a note that Groq
withdrew llama-3.3-70b-versatile mid-build (every call 404'd, failing silently
into a uniform distribution) and the pin moved to qwen/qwen3.8-27b — chosen over
the openai/gpt-oss-* models also on the roster because GPT-4o generated the
corpus and a judge from the generator's family would weaken separation rule 3.


================================================================================
9. RECOMMENDED ORDER OF WORK
================================================================================

    1.  3.1  reportability flag + choose real thresholds   (blocks all reporting)
    2.  3.2  parse_citations last-match + strip all        (wrong metric + leak)
    3.  3.4  fixed label set in encoder_vs_llm             (blocks model selection)
    4.  7    retrain the classifier                        (the actual bottleneck)
    5.  3.3  mask missed_examples                          (before results commit)
    6.  4.1  cap text length in detect_flags
    7.  4.3  resolve dead code
    8.       Stage 6 deliverables

Items 1-3 are prerequisites for reporting anything. Item 4 determines whether
there is a positive result to report at all.

================================================================================
END
================================================================================
